notes.title: USB audio, 2 or 10 channels
notes.text: USB audio, 2 or 10 channels: the FM-1 records into a computer over its USB cable (16-bit, 44.1 kHz), and MENU (hold HOME) > USB AUDIO now picks what it sends. 2 CH, the default, is the stereo master, exactly as before. 10 CH MIX sends the master on channels 1-2 and the eight tracks T1..T8 on channels 3-10, one mono channel each (each track before its PAN, the effect sends and the master effects). 10 CH FX sends the same eight tracks, with the chorus, delay and reverb returns on channels 1-2 instead of the master: pan the tracks in your DAW and add the effects pair to get the whole mix back, each part on its own fader.

notes.title: Switching
notes.text: Switching: 2 CH <-> 10 CH takes effect when the menu closes: the FM-1 leaves USB for about a second and comes back as the other device, "Hortator 8ch" in 10 CH (its channels named Main L, Main R, T1..T8). The sequencer and the sound play on; when following CLK USB the steps wait up to 2 s for the clock to come back. MIX <-> FX switches at once with a short cross-fade, no reconnect.

notes.title: Saved
notes.text: Saved: USB AUDIO is a device setting, saved and not part of projects; older settings start in 2 CH. A safe start (SEQ held at power-on) is always 2 CH.

notes.title: Computers
notes.text: Computers: the 10 channels work on macOS and iPadOS (class-compliant USB audio) and on Linux. Windows may not accept 10 CH: use 2 CH there.

notes.title: Bluetooth version
notes.text: Bluetooth version: 10 CH needs the standard build. The Bluetooth build is unchanged from 0.24.0: it has no USB AUDIO row, is always 2 CH and ignores a 10 CH setting saved by the standard build.

notes.title: Manual
notes.text: Manual: the landing page has a manual before the engines: a map of the panel (point at a control on a small FM-1, or at its line, to see what it does) and ten short guides (find your way, make a beat, shape a sound, play and record live, mute, perform, lock a step, save and chain, MIDI and LEARN, settings). Manual is in the top bar and the footer, and "More below" leads to it.
